name.en-US: Sermons on the Song of Songs
name.pt-BR: Sermões sobre o Cântico dos Cânticos

description.la: Octoginta et sex sermones quos Bernardus in capitulo Claraevallensi habuit, ab anno circiter 1135 usque ad mortem suam, de primis duobus Cantici capitibus: opus mysticum de unione animae cum Verbo. Textus ex editione Mabillonii in Migne (Patrologia Latina 183, 1854).
description.en-US: The eighty-six sermons Bernard preached to his monks at Clairvaux from about 1135 until his death, an allegorical commentary on the first two chapters of the Song of Songs and the great classic of medieval love mysticism: the soul’s union with the Word. Latin from the Maurist text in Migne (Patrologia Latina 183, 1854), a machine-corrected OCR; Mabillon’s note on the Evervin letter is kept at the end of Sermon 64. The English is that of a priest of Mount Melleray (Dublin, 1920), with his preface, notes and two appendices.
description.pt-BR: Os oitenta e seis sermões que Bernardo pregou aos seus monges em Claraval, a partir de cerca de 1135 até à morte, comentário alegórico dos dois primeiros capítulos do Cântico dos Cânticos e grande clássico da mística medieval do amor: a união da alma com o Verbo.

la.editor: Jean Mabillon, in J.-P. Migne (Patrologia Latina 183)

sources.edition: S. Bernardi Claraevallensis abbatis opera omnia, ed. J. Mabillon, in Migne, Patrologia Latina 183 (Paris 1854), Sermones in Cantica canticorum; TEI XML of the Corpus Corporum (University of Zurich), text 11258, from machine-corrected OCR.
sources.description: All eighty-six sermons. PL page breaks, column numbers and paragraph numbers are dropped; Scripture references stay in parentheses as printed. Mabillon’s editorial note on the Evervin letter, printed in the PL after Sermon 64, is kept at the end of that sermon. The OCR carries a few residual slips.
sources.tierEvidence: Bernard died in 1153; Migne’s 1854 printing is public domain everywhere.

sources.edition: St. Bernard's Sermons on the Canticle of Canticles, translated from the original Latin by a Priest of Mount Melleray, 2 vols. (Dublin: Browne and Nolan, 1920); archive.org stbernardssermon01bern and stbernardssermon02bern.
sources.description: Archive.org OCR read from the word-coordinate file and cleaned by script, not proofread: running heads and signature marks dropped, words broken at the gutter or misread repaired by a lexicon pass. About sixty pages the scan curled at the gutter were corrected by hand against the page images, and sermons XLII, XLIV and XLVII were re-read from the images with Tesseract. The translator's footnotes are kept, placed at their marker or, where the marker was lost, at the point the note stood on its page. The translator's preface and his two appendices (on the Sacred Heart; the glories of Saints Bernard and Augustine) are English-only chapters.
sources.tierEvidence: Published in 1920, before 1931: public domain in the US.
